info.title: tsuba — messenger adapter contract
info.summary: The HTTP + SSE surface every tsuba messenger adapter answers.
info.description:
One contract, one adapter per messenger. Each adapter is a local process holding one messenger account; a client written against this document works with any of them, and draws only what each one declares in `GET /capabilities`.

**Every response is an envelope.** Success carries `"ok": true` beside its payload; failure carries `"ok": false` and an `error` object with a machine-readable `code`. The HTTP status and the code say the same thing twice on purpose. `message` is for a person; branch on `code`, and keep a default branch because the set grows.

**Consumers must ignore keys they do not know.** Adding a key, a feature id or an error code is not breaking; removing or renaming one, or changing what an existing one means, is, and lands in a minor version with the reason in the changelog.

**Absent means unsupported.** A feature an adapter does not declare is not supported, and a client must not draw a control for it. An enum value a client does not know means the least that field can mean: treat it as the first value listed.

**Security posture.** A shared bearer token, loopback binding by default, and no TLS of its own; the token is a password to the user's messenger account. Reach it through SSH forwarding, a VPN, or a reverse proxy that terminates TLS and injects the header.

This version covers only the routes that are implemented: `/health` and `/capabilities`. Rooms, message reads, the stream and sending arrive with the code that answers them.

get.summary: Liveness, with no token, so a proxy can be checked apart from authentication.
What this adapter can do, and the limits its messenger enforces.
get.description: Like an AI API listing its models and what each supports. `revision` changes whenever anything else in the answer does, so a client can tell a held answer is stale. Today the features are network-wide; a room whose features differ will say so on the room itself once rooms are in this contract.

ErrorCode.description: Known codes. The set grows: keep a default branch.

version.description: The `info.version` of this document the adapter answers.
The adapter's own release, independent of the contract version.

id.description: Stable, e.g. `telegram`. Do not infer features from it; read `features`.

kind.description: `user`: the adapter acts as the person, seeing what their own client sees. `bot`: a bot account, seeing only where it was added. `official`: an official or business account. A client says which it is showing.

revision.description: Opaque content hash of the declaration.

Features.description: Supported features by id. Absent means unsupported. Ids under `x-<provider>.` are provider extensions; ignore any id you do not know.

rooms.list.description: List the conversations the account can see.

messages.read.description: Read a room's messages, oldest first.

paging.description: `none`: only the newest window. `before-id`: earlier pages before a message id.

resume.description: `none`: a reconnection starts from now. `cursor`: a reconnection resumes from per-room cursors without a gap.

maxLength.description: Longest text the messenger accepts, in Unicode code points.

receipt.description: `accepted`: the messenger took the request, nothing more is known. `stored`: the answer carries the id of the message the messenger stored.

messages.reply.description: Send a message as a reply to another.

messages.edit.description: Edit a message the account sent.

maxAgeSeconds.description: Absent when the messenger sets no age limit.

forEveryone.description: Whether deletion removes it for every participant rather than only this account.

maxPerMessage.description: Absent when the messenger sets no limit.

read.mark.description: Mark a room read up to a message, as the messenger's own client would.

typing.send.description: Show that the account is typing.

threads.read.description: Read a thread under a message. A thread is not a room; a room is the conversation.

maxBytes.description: Largest file the messenger accepts from this account.

caption.description: Whether a file can carry text with it.
